creator: Alexander Terp
description:
A `[[daemon]]` naming a machine that has never held a pane attaches, appears in the agent list, and cannot be used for anything. `muster window` says `devenv connected` and `no tabs, so this daemon is holding nothing`, and nothing in Muster can change that.

`open_remaining_regions` (`crates/muster-seam/src/session.rs:2544`) opens a region only for a daemon whose mirror has a focused tab, so one with no tabs is skipped. `open_a_workspace_if_the_window_is_empty` would ask for one, but it does not fire while the local daemon has tabs. That leaves making the pane by hand, and there is no way to say which machine it goes on: `CreateTab` carries a `daemon_id`, `cmd+t` calls `Core.createTab()` without one, and the CLI's `pane new` and `tab new` take a `--pane` to inherit from and nothing else.

Found attaching a devenv for the first time. The way through was `herdr workspace create` against the forwarded socket, after which everything behaves - the region opens on its own, the bridge comes up over ssh, and splits and tabs made from that pane stay on the box. So this is the first pane only, and only on a machine Muster has never made one on. It is also exactly the machine a new user has: "name an SSH host in your config and its agents appear in the same list" is true, and there is no way to put the first one there.

What the affordance should be is worth deciding before writing it. A `--daemon` on `tab new` is small and unlocks scripting. The window needs something else, because a person looking at an empty devenv section has no pane to split and nothing to focus - a row in the sidebar that opens one, or `open_remaining_regions` asking that daemon for a workspace the way the empty-window rule already asks the local one.

**It is not only a machine Muster has never touched.** Close the last local pane and the local daemon is in exactly the same state - `local connected`, `no tabs, so this daemon is holding nothing` - with the keyboard on a devenv pane and `cmd+t` making another devenv tab, because it resolves the daemon from where the keyboard is. Every route to a new pane in the window runs through an existing one: a split inherits its pane's daemon, a tab resolves one from the focused pane. So any daemon that reaches zero panes drops out of reach of the GUI, and the machine Muster is running on is no exception. Reached on a laptop within an hour of attaching a devenv for the first time, at which point the local machine could only be got back by making a pane with herdr or by editing the saved arrangement.

That makes the fix less about first contact and more about a permanent hole in the window's vocabulary: there is no way to say "a pane, on that machine". `CreateTab` already carries `daemon_id` and the sidebar already draws a row per machine, so both halves exist.

## Reproducing it

1. Attach two machines, or use one - it does not matter which is empty.
2. Empty a daemon of panes. In the window, close them; or from the CLI:

       HERDR=/Applications/Muster.app/Contents/Library/MusterSessions.app/Contents/MacOS/herdr
       HERDR_SOCKET_PATH=<that daemon's socket> $HERDR workspace list   # then close each
       HERDR_SOCKET_PATH=<that daemon's socket> $HERDR workspace close <id>

3. `muster window` now says `<daemon> connected` and `no tabs, so this daemon is holding nothing`.
4. Try to give it a pane without leaving Muster. `cmd+t` makes a tab on whichever machine the keyboard is on; a split inherits its pane's machine; `muster tab new` and `muster pane new` take a `--pane` to inherit from and no machine of their own. There is no route.

The same is true of a machine attached for the first time, which has never held a pane - that is how this was found.

## Validating a fix

- With a daemon holding nothing, a pane can be made on it from the window alone, and from `muster` alone, without touching `herdr`.
- The empty daemon is still visible while empty - see `a_2HtF52Itm`, where dropping the machine heading would take away the only evidence that an empty machine is attached at all.
- Worth testing with the *local* daemon emptied, not just a remote one: the two go through the same code and only the remote case is obvious.
- `CreateTab` already carries `daemon_id` and `resolve_daemon` falls back to the focused daemon when it is empty, so the wire has what it needs; the test is that something can populate it.
title: 🖥️ A daemon with no panes cannot be given one from the window
